# Daily routines with reflexive verbs

## Introduction

Spanish describes most of a morning with reflexive verbs: you wake yourself up, you shower yourself, you get yourself dressed. After this lesson you can tell someone what you do from the alarm to the front door, and follow a native speaker who describes their own routine. SpanishDict's guide sets out the pronouns and where they go ([SpanishDict: Reflexive verbs](https://www.spanishdict.com/guide/reflexive-verbs)).

## Lesson overview

- The reflexive pronouns me, te, se, nos and se.
- Where the pronoun sits: before a conjugated verb, joined to an infinitive.
- The routine verbs you need for a morning.
- Sequence words that order the steps of a day.

## Before you start

Answer these from what you already know. Check them in the sidecar after the assignment.

1. In "me levanto a las siete", who gets up, and what does "me" add?
2. How would you guess "she gets dressed" starts, from "vestirse"?

## Core idea

A reflexive verb names an action the subject does to itself. In the dictionary it ends in -se; when you conjugate it, the -se becomes a pronoun that matches the subject and moves in front of the verb ([SpanishDict: Reflexive verbs](https://www.spanishdict.com/guide/reflexive-verbs)).

```text
levantarse: me levanto, te levantas, se levanta, nos levantamos, se levantan
```

With an infinitive, the pronoun can join the end: "voy a levantarme".

## Words

| Word | Reading | Meaning | Example |
|------|---------|---------|---------|
| levantarse | - | to get up | Me levanto a las siete. |
| despertarse | - | to wake up | _Me despierto antes que mi hermana._ |
| ducharse | - | to shower | Me ducho por la mañana. |
| vestirse | - | to get dressed | _Se viste en cinco minutos._ |
| acostarse | - | to go to bed | Nos acostamos tarde. |
| desayunar | - | to have breakfast | Desayuno café y pan. |
| primero | - | first | Primero me ducho. |
| luego | - | then | Luego desayuno. |
| después | - | afterwards | Después salgo de casa. |
| temprano | - | early | Me levanto temprano. |

Source: [Wiktionary: Spanish frequency list](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Wiktionary:Frequency_lists/Spanish1000)

## Assignment

1. **[Dreaming Spanish on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@DreamingSpanish)**
   Why: native speakers describe their days at a pace you can follow.
   How: search the channel for "mi rutina" and watch one video at your level with Spanish subtitles on.
   Do: shadow the first two minutes, pausing after each sentence, then record yourself and compare.
2. **[SpanishDict: Reflexive verbs](https://www.spanishdict.com/guide/reflexive-verbs)**
   Why: the reference for the pronouns and where they go.
   How: read the sections on pronoun placement and skip the reciprocal uses for now.
   Do: write five sentences about your own morning, one per verb in the Words table.
3. **[Language Transfer: Complete Spanish](https://www.languagetransfer.org/complete-spanish)**
   Why: it builds sentences out loud from what you know.
   How: play the tracks on reflexive verbs and pause before each answer.
   Do: answer every prompt aloud before the speaker does.
